title: RAW UNREVIEWED: Pliny verbenaca: two morphologies share effects without becoming reproductive sexes
summary: RAW_UNREVIEWED_NOT_SELECTED_NOT_TESTED. Pliny distinguishes densely and sparsely leafed varieties called female and male, while reporting that some authorities unite them because their effects are the same. Keep morphological distinction and therapeutic equivalence as separate predicates over two botanical varieties. Preserve the reported disagreement between classifications.

source.span: Volume V, chapter 59, Hierabotane/peristereon/verbenaca, first descriptive paragraph
source.observed_content: Pliny distinguishes densely and sparsely leafed varieties called female and male, while reporting that some authorities unite them because their effects are the same.
source.layer: Modern edition/translation of an ancient primary work; source-only exploratory input, not a newly collated medieval witness

potential_admitted_target: Already-admitted f6v/f9v paired-entry work is only a potential comparison set; no verbenaca identity or matched plant pair is assumed.

design.mechanism: Keep morphological distinction and therapeutic equivalence as separate predicates over two botanical varieties. Preserve the reported disagreement between classifications.
design.unit: Entire descriptive source paragraph, including the attribution to unnamed authorities, then two complete target plant records if independently eligible.
design.contrast: Identity everywhere erases morphology; different efficacy everywhere erases the shared-effect claim; reproductive-sex interpretation adds a causal relation the selected paragraph does not state.
design.prediction: A reading should permit different descriptions with a shared efficacy statement without merging plant identity or importing fertilisation. The same form must not mean literal SAME_PLANT in one clause and SAME_EFFECT in another without written scope.
design.scope: Source-only raw proposal; no selected manuscript content, assigned glosses or executed experiment

execution_requirements: Review the complete f6v/f9v predecessors before proposing any target pair and retain the failed identification/ownership limits.
Bind both variants and their shared predicate using a source-owned medieval entry; a common leaf shape is insufficient.
A target needs two explicitly owned records with usable shared construction, not merely a male/female picture.
assumptions_and_limits: No Voynich word receives a meaning from this proposal.
An ancient work in a modern edition supplies historical content, not a medieval manuscript owner or independent Voynich binding.
The named target is a potential already-admitted locus, not a claim that its image or text contains the required roles. Root must verify the exact admission and ownership before selection.
A new scored relation packet requires capacity, held-folio, provenance and mobile-null gates; no reserve or f84/f84r access.
